summary: Mud Lake Wildlife Refuge fire tower, built 1939 by USFWS; county survey ties it to a refuge HQ tower that the FFLOS index marks gone; sources disagree.

facts.design: Wood tower with enclosed crow's nest, 110 ft (1941 survey notes); another note in the same survey says about 100 ft and wood, and that other records report a 100 ft steel tower
facts.status_note: Original Mud Lake site: tower gone per FFLOS index. County survey points to the present refuge headquarters tower as the successor; the index marks that HQ tower gone; sources disagree

access.note: County survey says the HQ tower is standing and open to the public. A refuge brochure labelled 2000 says use is permitted in snow-free months during office hours, with a key from the office. No newer access source read.

corrections.why: The county survey says the tower stood in the refuge under its old name and points to the present tower at refuge headquarters. The FFLOS index marks the headquarters tower as gone, so an editor should check the current state before accepting this change.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The county survey gives 1939 for the Mud Lake tower; a note in the Agassiz entry gives 1938. The story uses 1939 from the survey table and reports the 1938 note.
1941 survey notes say wood, 110 ft; the Agassiz entry note says wood, about 100 ft; other records report a 100 ft steel tower. The story reports each version.

sources.title: Agassiz National Wildlife Refuge brochure (file labelled 2000)

notes_for_editor: The name Webster Creek appears only in the FFLOS index; no county or refuge source read uses it. The Mud Lake coordinates match the index, so the record is the same site. The index marks the Agassiz HQ tower gone while the county survey says standing; check current status with the refuge before publishing the relocated status. The brochure date comes from its file label (2000) only. The link between the 1939 Mud Lake tower and the HQ tower rests on the county survey's own notes. No photos. Two web searches used.
